title: Wave 1: one reliable delivery path (roadmap 2026-09-10)
description:
Wave 1 of the 2026-09-10 improvement roadmap (Downloads/Moes-Tavern-Improvement-Roadmap.md, sections 1 and 2). Goal: make DONE mean the code was actually delivered, and make ownership survive a restart.

Today complete_task validates a worker-reported verification object without running the command or binding it to a revision, qa_approve explicitly allows DONE with no completion commit (a soft NO-COMPLETION-COMMIT warning), and the wrapper lands bytes only after the CLI exits. The roadmap author reproduced the consequence against the real handlers: task A reaches DONE with completionCommits empty, and a worker then successfully claims a task that depends on A. Separately, daemon startup calls purgeAllWorkers without establishing that the external CLI processes exited, so a restart during a long build hands a live worker's task to someone else.

Wave 1 introduces six records and the rules that bind them: plan revision, execution attempt, candidate, check run, review and delivery receipt. It is deliberately ONE narrow end-to-end pilot, not a framework: one repository, one configured delivery target, one supported provider mode, shared daemon/runner/client fixtures. Provider and platform coverage expands later through explicit contract tests.

Acceptance for the epic as a whole, taken from the roadmap: fast QA cannot finish before candidate preparation; a failed required gate cannot release dependents; reviewing candidate A cannot approve B; restarting only the daemon during a long build preserves ownership; delayed generation-N calls cannot alter generation N+1; a crash between an external effect and its bookkeeping does not repeat the effect blindly.
architectureNotes:
The daemon stays the sole state authority and the wrapper stays the only git and process actor — Wave 1 must not move git into the daemon. Extend the existing .moe/ JSON store; no database migration is a prerequisite. Copy the durable-first pattern already proven in state/resourceStore.ts: persist the authoritative record before the state transition it enables, repair partial transitions on a later pass, and support holder/generation preconditions on release.

Attempt generation is the fencing token for daemon mutations only. It does not stop an old CLI from writing shared files, so reassignment must first establish that the old process stopped or contain its writes in a separate workspace. The same caveat applies to leases: a JSON record cannot stop a running external job.

Keep the existing rule that a quiet build is not evidence of a dead worker. There is deliberately no idle-based auto-release for WORKING/PLANNING and Wave 1 must not reintroduce one; heartbeats should instead distinguish process presence, provider presence, waiting for input and observed progress, and tell a runner when reattachment is required.

Preserve autoCommit=false and manual/no-git projects: missing code evidence must be labelled as such, never silently reported as verified delivery.
epicRails: One narrow vertical slice: one repository, one delivery target, one provider mode. No abstract framework and no wholesale launcher rewrite before the slice proves the contract.
The daemon remains state-only and never runs git; the wrapper/runner remains the only git and process actor.
Extend the existing .moe/ JSON store using the resourceStore durable-first pattern. A database migration is not a prerequisite and must not be introduced here.
Every change lands with a test that fails on the old behaviour.
Do not break autoCommit=false, manual/no-git projects, or the rule that a quiet build is not evidence of a dead worker.
